question.problem:
$$
{∭}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{∗}{\int }_{∗}^{∗}{\int }_{∗}^{b}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx
$$

The triple integral above is defined over the type III region given by

$$
S=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,-2\le z\le {x}^{2}+2,\,-2-z\le y\le 2+x+z\}.
$$

What is the value of $a-b?$
question.worked_solution:
A type III region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,{u}_{1}(x,z)\le y\le {u}_{2}(x,z)\}.
$$

A typical three-dimensional type III region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217845/assets/0603bed12c6af74e46544d8bebc52362aed95a9a5ad7418ea4faaf228f3b5241.png)

 

If $R$ is a type III region, we can express the triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ as a mixed integral, as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y]\,\text{d}A
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{u}_{1}(x,z)=-2-z,\,{u}_{2}(x,z)=2+x+z.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
{∭}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-2-z}^{2+x+z}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dA.
$$

 

Now, the region $D$ is given by

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,-2\le z\le {x}^{2}+2\}.
$$

Therefore, by expressing the double integral over $D$ as a repeated integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-2-z}^{2+x+z}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-2}^{{x}^{2}+2}[{\int }_{-2-z}^{2+x+z}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dz\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-2}^{{x}^{2}+2}{\int }_{-2-z}^{2+x+z}f(x,y,z)\,dy\,dz\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a-b=(0)-(2+x+z)=-2-x-z.
$$
